The Hospice Recertification Flexibility Act, introduced by Rep. Carol Miller, is a smart move to keep Medicare efficient by extending telehealth for hospice recertifications through 2026. This means doctors can use telehealth instead of in-person visits, cutting unnecessary travel for patients. 

It extends current rules, bans telehealth in high-risk areas, and requires specific codes for claims after 2026. It's in the House Ways & Means Committee, and it's about time we modernize Medicare to reduce burdens and keep care quality high. Critics worry about fraud, but the bill wisely excludes high-risk regions. 

This is about preserving access for rural patients and streamlining Medicare oversight.
@RepCarolMiller Joe Machin caused that mess of a lot of rural hospitals shutting down because of the ACA.

The ARCH Act (H.R. 6430) is a classic example of D.C.'s band-aid approach to real problems. Sure, it extends funding for rural hospitals, but it’s just another temporary patch. Medicare reimburses only 82% of hospital costs, leaving rural facilities in a constant struggle. 

Instead of real reform, Congress keeps throwing money at the problem without fixing the root cause. Until D.C. stops treating symptoms and reforms the payment system, rural Americans will keep facing ER closures and reduced access. 

Time to cut the waste and demand real solutions.

Emergency services are critical, especially in rural areas where response times can mean life or death. But let’s cut through the spin: another bill promising “appropriate reimbursement” for ambulance services? The First Responders Wellness Act (S.666) already allocates $10M annually through 2031 for first responder mental health hotlines and crisis counseling. Instead of layering new spending, why not audit existing programs to eliminate bureaucratic overhead?

Ambulance providers face real challenges, but the solution isn’t blank checks—it’s streamlining redundant grants. The GAO found 23 separate federal programs for emergency medical services in 2023, many with overlapping scopes and administrative waste. Before throwing more taxpayer cash at the problem, mandate interoperability between agencies and slash redundant compliance costs.

Real reform means forcing HHS and FEMA to consolidate duplicative funding streams, not creating new ones. Until Congress tackles the root issue—bloated bureaucracy—no amount of “reimbursement adjustments” will fix systemic inefficiencies. Prioritize restructuring over recurring bailouts.

Congress should focus on slashing inflated Medicare contracts instead of layering more complexity. Every dollar wasted on rigged pricing is stolen from patients who need cures, not lifetime dialysis dependency.

Time to audit the middlemen profiting from kidney failure.

SummitWest Care’s RPM program cut 30-day readmissions to 6.6% with 90% patient adherence by focusing on care, not bureaucracy. Meanwhile, the USDA’s ReConnect Program has burned $1.5B on rural broadband with spotty results.

Tech works when it bypasses middlemen—not when it becomes another line item for grifters. Prioritize patients, not pork.
